headline._ppi_note: PPI++/EIF rectifier (arXiv:2601.05420): gpt52=prediction (covers all reports), full panel=gold label; mu_ppi=mean(pred)+mean(gold-pred|labelled). Companion to mean_3judge, not a replacement.
headline._ppi_caveat: IMPORTANT: the PPI 'gold' anchor is the PANEL MEAN, not external truth/gold. So this is PANEL-anchored debiasing (gpt52 -> panel mean), NOT truth/gold-anchored debiasing. For the full-panel patterns (every report scored by all panel judges, n_unlabelled=0) the rectifier is ALGEBRAICALLY the raw panel mean_3judge (mean(pred)+mean(panel-pred)=mean(panel)), so PPI does NO real work there; it corrects gpt52->panel and does real work ONLY on the 2 REDUCED-PANEL patterns (base_p11, base_p12; 2-judge panels with many unlabelled reports), where the abundant gpt52 predictions extend the panel-mean estimate onto reports the reduced panel never scored. (p1/p3 carry only a stray 1-report gap on an otherwise full 3-judge panel and are effectively full-panel.) This is the lambda=1 rectifier (rectifier applied in full), NOT lambda-tuned PPI++.

rxu_decomposition._note: Claim-level factual decomposition P(correct)=P(R)xP(U|R). R = a source was retrieved for the claim (claim is not no_source); U|R = the retrieved source actually supports the claim. P(correct) equals the C0/E14 verified factual accuracy by construction. Claim-pooled over reports. gpt52 judge feeds the headline scores; the claim/entailment labels are the C0 pipeline (PTU gpt-4o, deployment sthree-ptu-02, $0 marginal, NO Opus, NO 7B).

rxu_conditional._note: Utilisation re-expressed as a CONDITIONAL, not a flat ratio, per DeepResearch-Slice. Per claim: R = retrieved-evidence present in the saved NLI snapshot (verdict != no_source); U|R = entailment match among retrieved (verdict == supports). accuracy = mean(R) * mean(U|R) per pattern. Replaces component_eval.py:286 (cited/available, and n_supports/n_claims) which conflates the retrieval-bound and utilisation-bound shares of the factual gap.
rxu_conditional.verifier: citation_verifier NLI mode (deep_research/evaluation/citation_verifier.py); claim-level SAFE/FActScore entailment, PTU gpt-4o C0 pipeline

definitions.R: 1 if a retrieved snapshot was present (verdict in supports|neutral|contradicts) else 0
definitions.U_given_R: among R==1 claims, 1 if verdict == supports (entailment match) else 0
definitions.decomposition: the informative pair is (mean_R, mean_U|R); their product == n_supports/n_claims (the flat ratio) and is reported as support_rate for reference only

judge_vs_gold.cross_family_finding: On the MATCHED common report set (n=259 reports scored by all panel judges), GPT-5.2's factual verdicts are answer-sensitive (common-set AUC 0.6483) while both Claude judges are near-chance. The cross-family AUC gap is now backed by a paired DeLong test on the SAME reports (it previously compared different per-judge report sets, untested): gpt52>opus diff=0.107 (DeLong p=0.031337), gpt52>sonnet diff=0.1566 (DeLong p=0.000275); both significant at .05 under DeLong. Under the conservative query-CLUSTERED paired bootstrap, however, ONLY gpt52-vs-sonnet survives (cluster CI [0.0396, 0.273], excludes 0); the gpt52-vs-opus asymmetry DISSOLVES under clustering (cluster CI [-0.0021, 0.2172] INCLUDES 0). So the robust, clustering-surviving cross-family finding is gpt52>sonnet alone; the opus arm rests on DeLong only. The answer signal reflects general report completeness, not factual-dimension specificity; the load-bearing result is the gpt52-vs-sonnet cross-family validity asymmetry, matched-set, difference-tested, and clustering-robust.

calibration._note: P2_judge_kappa: chance-corrected AGREEMENT (weighted Cohen kappa + Krippendorff alpha) of each judge's thresholded factual_accuracy vs the human gold slice, reported ALONGSIDE the existing rank-only AUCs in per_judge. AUC measures discrimination (ranking correct>incorrect); kappa/alpha measure whether the judge assigns the SAME label as the gold net of chance, at a fixed judge-internal operating point. Per arXiv:2510.09738, a high AUC can co-exist with poor kappa; this block lets a reader see both. Same LitQA2+DeepSearchQA slice as judge_vs_gold (n's match n_reports_with_gold). Anchors, does not certify (general mechanical gold, small slice). Two pre-stated discretisations (binary at median; ordinal3 at tertiles) reported, no post-hoc selection.
calibration.operating_point_note: thresholds are JUDGE-internal score quantiles (median / tertiles); they do NOT use the gold labels, so agreement is not tuned upward.
calibration.headline: Even the answer-sensitive judge (GPT-5.2: factual AUC 0.6587) shows chance-corrected agreement of only kappa(binary)=0.1716 [poor], weighted-kappa(ordinal)=0.1417 [poor] vs the human gold slice — below the 0.60 substantial band and far below the ~0.85 high-stakes floor. This is the arXiv:2510.09738 high-AUC/low-kappa illusion on our own panel: ranking is not agreement.

variance_decomposition._note: E2 replicate variance for live-retrieval long-form report agents. Run+query variance from the gpt52 replicate corpus (P0 x11, 7 arch x3, 30 queries); judge variance is in `variance_components` (panel), NOT crossed with run here. First full-pipeline replicate variance study for live-retrieval long-form report agents (cf. Wang 2512.21326 short-form; ICC 2512.06710 GAIA-only). Prereg: prereg_E2.md.
variance_decomposition.single_judge_caveat: replicate corpus is gpt52-only; run and judge variance are on non-crossed substrates; fully-crossed run x judge is the extension.
variance_decomposition.bayes_companion_note: each entry in `components` carries a `bayes_halfcauchy` companion: posterior median + 95% credible interval for sigma_run and sigma_query from a one-way random-effects Gibbs sampler with half-Cauchy(0,0.50) priors on the SDs (Gelman 2006; arXiv:2509.00636). Reported ALONGSIDE the REML point estimates so the small-n (n_reps=3) run-noise interval does not rest on REML/Wald asymptotics. The Bayes medians track the REML points (e.g. base_p0: REML sigma_run 0.0488 vs Bayes 0.0489), while the credible intervals widen sharply for the ragged-coverage arches (p5/p6/p8), as expected at low replicate/query support. Per-arch deterministic seed via SHA-256 of arch name.

run_noise.anchor: base_p0 (11 replicates) is the most precise run-noise estimate

flip_rates.aggregation_note: overall is the MACRO-average over the 9 dimensions (mean of per-dimension means); a flat micro-average over all criterion cells is ~0.075.

citation_stability.note: CV of citation COUNT across replicates; set-level overlap needs report parsing (text not in parquet) and is deferred.

mde.interpretation: smallest true overall-score gap an n-query, r-replicate paired design can detect at 80% power given run noise alone.

leaderboard_flip.resampling_unit: run (one actual replicate pattern per architecture)
leaderboard_flip.note: single ACTUAL-run ranking vs all-replicate 'true' ranking over the full-coverage architectures (gpt52, 30 variance queries). Run-level resampling (not cell-level), so run noise is NOT averaged away. The five fully-covered architectures are well-separated (gaps >> MDE80), so their single-run ranking is stable; this does NOT generalise to near-tied architectures (see all_arches_companion and the MDE result).

all_arches_companion.caveat: includes p5/p6/p8 whose single runs cover only 8-18 of 30 queries (ranks partly confounded by coverage); the lower tau shows the near-tie architecture cluster reorders under run noise, consistent with MDE80=0.025 > the within-cluster gaps.

three_way._note: 3-way crossed run x query x judge variance decomposition. EXTENDS variance_decomposition (gpt52-only run facet) by ingesting the on-disk Sonnet-4.6 replicate verdicts (judge_claude_sonnet48/base_p*_v*) and fitting the crossed REML on the balanced gpt52-and-sonnet intersection. No new judging (Sonnet verdicts read from disk); no paid API. Addresses single_judge_caveat: run and judge variance are now on a CROSSED substrate (limited to the 2-judge intersection).
three_way.recompute: overall_score_recomputed (source-type weights), identical to build_analysis_dataframes; Sonnet stored overall_score is corrupted and NOT used.

coverage.caveat: Sonnet replicate coverage is THINNER and UNBALANCED vs gpt52: gpt52 scores P0 x11 reps over 30 variance queries (7 further arch x3); Sonnet covers fewer queries per cell (e.g. P0: 27 of 30). Sonnet's STORED overall_score is corrupted upstream, so both judges use overall_score_recomputed (source-type weights, identical to build_analysis_dataframes; self-checked to <1e-6 vs the gpt52 parquet). The crossed REML below is fit on the BALANCED INTERSECTION scored by BOTH judges; gpt52-only rows are dropped from the fit and reported here.

intersection.design: fully crossed run x query within the two-level judge factor (gpt52, sonnet48)

reml_3way.model: MixedLM REML, score ~ 1 + (1|arch) + (1|run) + (1|query) + (1|judge), crossed (run nested in arch)
reml_3way.correction_note: B3 review fix: added (1|arch) so sigma2_run is within-architecture replicate noise, not arch-confounded run share.
fit_warnings: The MLE may be on the boundary of the parameter space.

cross_judge_anchor.note: Judge facet has only TWO levels (gpt52, sonnet48), so the REML judge variance component is a single between-judge contrast and is estimated with low precision; the per-judge means and paired-cell correlation are reported as a robust, identification-free companion to sigma2_judge.

three_way.limitations: (1) judge facet = 2 levels only -> sigma2_judge is a single contrast, low precision; (2) fit on the balanced intersection, so power is set by the Sonnet (thinner) coverage; (3) Sonnet source is claude_code_manual; (4) this is the crossed EXTENSION, not a replacement for the gpt52 run-facet estimate in variance_decomposition.components.

bootstrap_ci._note: P2_var_bootstrap (Paper 3): B=2000 PARAMETRIC (Gaussian) bootstrap percentile CIs for the REML variance components (sigma2_query, sigma2_run, ICC_query) of overall_score_recomputed ~ 1 | query_id, per architecture, on the gpt52 variance-replicate corpus. Replaces the Wald/point-only `components` output with model-based bootstrap intervals (query REs ~ N(0,sigma2_query), residuals ~ N(0,sigma2_run) resampled on the SAME observed design, REML refit each draw). Standard LMM variance-component interval per lme4::confint(method='boot'/'profile'); percentile-CI practice for eval-variance follows arXiv:2509.00255 and arXiv:2306.10779. Appends `bootstrap_ci`; leaves `components` (point estimates) untouched.
bootstrap_ci.data_sufficiency: 5 full-coverage architectures (30 queries x >=3 reps) give tight CIs; ragged architectures (p5=14q, p6=8q, p8=18q x 3 reps) give WIDE CIs with sigma2_query draws near the >=0 boundary, reported per-arch via `coverage` — this is exactly why parametric bootstrap percentile intervals replace the boundary-violating Wald intervals.

bayes_crosscheck._note: Non-CLT Bayesian beta-binomial cross-check (bayes_evals style) of the two small-n equivalence/precision claims: the n=6 oracle-factual t-TOST (+/-0.05) and the CLT-based MDE80 run-noise scale (n=3-11 cells). Emitted ALONGSIDE the CLT/t numbers so the +/-0.05 equivalence does not rest solely on the n=6 CLT interval.
bayes_crosscheck.citation: Bowyer, Aitchison & Ivanova, 'Position: Don't Use the CLT in LLM Evals' (bayes_evals), ICML 2025, arXiv:2503.01747; Miller, 'Adding Error Bars to Evals', arXiv:2411.00640.
bayes_crosscheck.caveat: Bayesian beta-binomial intervals are model-based (Beta(1,1) prior, verdicts treated as exchangeable Bernoulli within a cell; not query-clustered); they corroborate the CLT/t equivalence at +/-0.05 but are not a substitute for the pre-registered TOST.

bayes_oracle_factual_tost.method: Beta(1,1)-prior Beta-Binomial posterior on the per-(pattern) factual_accuracy SATISFIED counts; cluster-mean delta = mean of the 6 per-pattern (oracle-base) rate-difference posteriors. Bayesian analogue of oracle.factual_tost; uses NO Normal/t quantile and NO n=6 df=5 SE (integrates ~2900 Bernoulli verdicts pooled across both conditions, ~1440 oracle-side + ~1432 base-side; corrected 2026-07-28, adversarial review round 21 -- this note previously said only ~1440, the oracle side alone).
bayes_oracle_factual_tost.prior: Beta(1,1) uniform (bayes_evals default); Jeffreys Beta(0.5,0.5) shifts the equivalence probability by <0.01 at these counts and is not reported separately.
bayes_oracle_factual_tost.agreement_with_clt_tost: concordant: CLT t-TOST gives equivalent@+/-0.05 (p_tost=0.0153) and NOT@+/-0.02; the Beta-Binomial posterior likewise places high mass within +/-0.05 and clearly fails +/-0.02 (see probabilities). The +/-0.05 equivalence therefore does not rest on the n=6 CLT interval alone (Bowyer 2503.01747; Miller 2411.00640).

clt_vs_bayes_mde._note: Sanity-check that the CLT machinery underlying MDE80 (Z=z_.975+z_.80 on run noise from n=3-11 replicate cells) is not anti-conservative at this n. Compares a Normal 94% interval and a Beta-Binomial 94% credible interval on the pooled replicate criterion-DISAGREEMENT rate (the binary process that GENERATES run noise).
clt_vs_bayes_mde.verdict: Beta-Binomial and Normal 94% intervals on the run-noise-generating flip rate are within a few percent of each other (the flip pool is large, n_pairs>>10), so the MDE80 CLT scale is not anti-conservative here; the small-n CLT concern bites on the n=6 oracle-mean TOST, which §1 above re-derives without the CLT.

e5_crosscheck._note: Beta-Binomial non-CLT re-derivation of e5_equivalence.factual_flat (g100_minus_g000 factual within +/-0.05; pooled P0/P1/P4). Counts from raw GPT-5.2 e5 verdict JSONs. Bayesian analogue of the e5 t-TOST/CLT interval.
e5_crosscheck.contrast: g100_minus_g000 (full oracle-dose range), factual_accuracy SATISFIED rate
e5_crosscheck.agreement_with_clt: concordant with e5_equivalence.factual_flat (CLT TOST p_tost=0.0, ci90 within +/-0.05): the Beta-Binomial posterior also concentrates within +/-0.05.

n_eff._note: E3 effective judge count at criterion-verdict level on the fully-crossed 3-panel cell. N_eff = 9/(3+2*sum phi). Within-family (opus-sonnet) vs cross-family (gpt52-Claude) agreement per dimension. CARE/Ising aggregation deferred. Prereg: prereg_E3.md.
n_eff.robustness_note_ac1: phi (Pearson on 0/1 verdicts) is prevalence-attenuated when judges have very different positive rates; Gwet's AC1 is reported ALONGSIDE as a prevalence-robust companion for the excess and the per-dimension ranking. Per-dimension excess tests are paired query-clustered bootstraps (seed=20260611, N=2000) Holm-corrected across the 9 dimensions, for both phi and AC1. The overall within-minus-cross excess is phi=+0.158 / AC1=+0.316; the artefact signature holds under the prevalence-robust statistic iff the AC1 ranking + Holm-significant dimensions agree (see artefact_signature_ranking_ac1).
n_eff.ranking_note: Top within-minus-cross dimensions: instruction_following (0.2724) ~ logical_coherence (0.2609) at the top (a near-tie), then citation_quality (0.2033). citation_quality is genuinely ELEVATED and positive but ranks THIRD, not second/first; a query-clustered bootstrap (adversarial review 2026-06-11) places it significantly below both dimensions above it. So headline (iii)'s citation-specific prediction is only PARTIALLY borne out: the two Claudes are redundant (N_eff<3) and citation IS one of the elevated dimensions, but it is not THE signature; instruction_following and logical_coherence lead.
n_eff.interpretation: N_eff < 3 => the two Claude judges are partially redundant. The dimensions with the largest within_minus_cross (instruction_following, logical_coherence) are where the two-Claude correlation most exceeds cross-family; citation_quality is elevated (third) but not the leading signature (see ranking_note).

within_openai._note: T1 within-OpenAI N_eff control cell. Self-contained: reads judge JSON dirs directly; criterion_id == md5[:12] of normalised criterion text, identical to build_analysis_dataframes.py. within_openai.interpretation: Same-lab redundancy: within-OpenAI mean phi = 0.4181 (N_eff_openai = 1.4104 over 2 judges); within-Anthropic mean phi = 0.512 (N_eff_anthropic = 1.3227). Cross-family mean phi = 0.396. If within-family phi >> cross-family phi for BOTH labs, judge redundancy is a same-lab effect symmetric across families, not a Claude-specific artefact; if only Anthropic collapses, the headline within-Claude redundancy is family-specific. diagnostics._note: P2 N_eff/k saturation flag + Condorcet-null panel contrast. n_eff_over_k = n_eff.overall.n_eff / k flagged against the arXiv:2605.29800 N_eff/k < 0.5 saturation rule (do NOT add a 4th correlated LLM judge). condorcet_null contrasts the observed correlated panel against a same-marginal INDEPENDENT panel on the SAME 36,113 crossed cells (build_n_eff.py cell): the Condorcet Jury Theorem's reliability gains require independence, so the observed-minus-null excess unanimity quantifies the redundancy that drives N_eff << k. Closed-form is canonical; seeded Monte-Carlo (SEED=20260611) only corroborates.
diagnostics.saturation_note: N_eff/k = 0.5516 for the 3-judge panel (N_eff=1.6547). The arXiv:2605.29800 caution fires at N_eff/k < 0.5; this panel sits JUST ABOVE that line (one correlated judge short of saturation). Either way the operational reading is the same: a 4th LLM judge drawn from the same correlated pool would add far less than one independent vote, so the panel should NOT be grown by adding a 4th correlated judge.

condorcet_null._note: Observed correlated panel vs simulated-independent (Condorcet) panel on the 36,113 crossed cells; same marginal SATISFIED rates, zero correlation.

diagnostics.interpretation: On the same 36,113 crossed cells, the real panel reaches unanimity 0.5265 of the time, but three INDEPENDENT judges with the same marginal rates would agree only 0.2527 of the time (excess +0.2738); per-judge agreement with the majority is likewise inflated (0.8422 observed vs 0.7521 independent). The Condorcet Jury Theorem's reliability gains assume independence, so this correlation-driven excess is exactly why N_eff (1.6547) is far below k (3) and N_eff/k = 0.5516 hugs the arXiv:2605.29800 saturation line. The naive 'add another judge' move buys almost no independent information: do NOT add a 4th correlated LLM judge.

model_recall._note: Model-recall / win-multiplicity decomposition of the oracle gap on the replicate matrix (gpt52, variance family, 8 archs x 30 queries; replicates averaged). PRIMARY is the complete-case dense 30x5 subset (p0,p1,p10,p4,p7 — present on all 30 queries; p5,p6,p8 are sparse and excluded to avoid a selection-biased Best-Single, mirroring build_routability's exclusion of p2/p3/p9). Re-labels random/best-fixed/oracle as Random/Best-Single/Oracle and reports Gain@R, Gain@B (=Best-Single mean), Gap@O (=Oracle-Best-Single). Win-multiplicity = #archs within EPS of the per-query max; single_winner_fraction at EPS=0.01 is the % of queries whose oracle gain is an unrecoverable unique-winner label. Strengthens G1: the oracle headroom is concentrated in single-winner queries, so a feature router cannot recall it out of sample — complementary to the noise-capitalisation null in routability.replicate_cv. Framing per LLMRouterBench (arXiv:2601.07206). Appends as routability.model_recall.
model_recall.citation: arXiv:2601.07206 (LLMRouterBench): Random vs Best-Single vs Oracle routing; realizable router gain over Best-Single shrinks as win-multiplicity falls.

headroom_concentration.interpretation: At EPS=0.01, 90% of the 30 primary queries have a UNIQUE winner (win-multiplicity 1). The oracle headroom over Best-Single is 0.044 in those single-winner queries vs 0.0026 in the multiplicity>=2 queries: the gap lives almost entirely in unique-winner queries, where the routing target is a high-entropy per-query label. This is the model-recall reason the raw oracle gain is not realizable out of sample (a feature router cannot recover a unique-winner label), corroborating routability.replicate_cv_headroom (~0.003) and the G1 null framing.

model_recall.g1_relevance: Supports G1 NULL: high single-winner fraction => oracle gap is an unrecoverable per-query label, not a routable feature-conditioned signal.

Per-pattern faithfulness = 1 - suspect/tested. Pure replay on saved trajectories; no model calls. CONDITIONAL: strict LOSO needs saved multi-chunk context + saved remainder NLI verdicts; if absent, strict block is `data_insufficient` and a labelled on-disk lower-bound proxy is reported instead.
citation_faithfulness.citation_finding: ~57% of LLM long-form citations are post-hoc rationalisations.

strict_loso.reason: Strict LOSO faithfulness requires, per cited claim, (i) the multi-chunk retrieved context and (ii) a SAVED NLI verdict of the claim against the leave-one-out remainder. df_c0_verdicts.parquet stores one evidence_quote per claim with ~1 row per (pattern,query,claim) and no remainder re-test; citation_verify.json snapshots are aggregate stubs. Neither is a replay substrate, so the strict metric is NOT computable at $0 from on-disk data.
strict_loso.to_materialise: Run a dedicated LOSO replay (citation_verifier.nli_verify_batch over claim x remainder-context) and persist per-cited-claim {own_chunk_verdict, loso_remainder_verdict} to the missing parquet; this builder then computes per-pattern faithfulness with no further calls.

proxy_lowerbound.definition: Among CITED claims (citation_idx non-null), the share whose own cited source does NOT entail the claim (verdict in {neutral,no_source,contradicts}). This is a LOWER BOUND on post-rationalisation (misses the LOSO case where the cited chunk entails but the remainder also does), hence an UPPER BOUND on faithfulness. NOT the headline metric.

citation_faithfulness.interpretation: If/when the LOSO replay parquet is materialised, a per-pattern faithfulness rate well below 1 (≈0.43 if the arXiv:2412.18004 ~57% post-rationalisation rate replicates here) would show citations are largely decorative rather than load-bearing — sharpening the paper's 'bounded returns to orchestration' claim on the citation channel. Until then the on-disk PROXY gives a labelled bound only.

headline_replicated._what: Re-rank of the P0-P12 architecture headline on REPLICATE-AVERAGED GPT-5.2 judged scores, to defend the single-run headline against the E2 run-variance self-contradiction. Substrate: judge=gpt52, query set = E2 30-query variance subset (held constant single-run vs replicate-averaged).

substrate.note_3judge_90q: the 3-judge / 90-query headline panel is a different substrate; this is a within-gpt52, within-q30 ranking robustness check, NOT a re-derivation of that panel.

headline_replicated.method_note: Two-level paired bootstrap (n_boot=10000, seed=20260622): OUTER resamples the common query set (paired across patterns); INNER resamples replicate runs within each (pattern,query) cell with replacement then averages, propagating run-to-run noise. cluster_vs_p0_survives is the RUN-NOISE ROBUSTNESS verdict from clean_substrate.run_noise_robustness: on all full-coverage members {p1,p4,p7,p8} + P0 on ONE shared 30q substrate, does replicate-averaging PRESERVE the single-run member-vs-P0 separation structure (sign of gap AND Holm verdict)? If yes, the single-run ranking is not a run-noise artefact (refuting the E2 self-contradiction). The load-bearing headline claim (top-3 {p1,p4,p7} each Holm-separate above P0) is surfaced as clean_substrate.top_performers_claim.top_performers_separate_from_p0. p8 is included and disclosed (rank-5 above P0 on the 3-judge 90q panel, but below P0 on this gpt52-only 30q subset in BOTH single-run and replicate-averaged => a substrate/judge effect, not run-noise; see p8_substrate_disclosure). Separation = one-sided member>P0 with joint Holm (alpha=0.05); tie = TOST-style pair CI within +/-0.05. Ragged members p5/p6 (8-14q) are descriptive only. holm() identical to build_pairwise.py.

base_p2.note: NO judged replicate runs (single canonical judged run only) -> follow-up: judge the on-disk replicate report runs.

base_p3.note: NO judged replicate runs (single canonical judged run only) -> follow-up: judge the on-disk replicate report runs.

base_p9.note: NO judged replicate runs (single canonical judged run only) -> follow-up: judge the on-disk replicate report runs.

base_p12.note: NO judged replicate runs (single canonical judged run only) -> follow-up: judge the on-disk replicate report runs.

clean_substrate.note: RUN-NOISE ROBUSTNESS test on ALL full-coverage cluster members ['base_p1', 'base_p4', 'base_p7', 'base_p8'] vs P0 on ONE shared 30-query substrate (judge=gpt52). p8 is INCLUDED (full 3-replicate coverage) and disclosed, NOT dropped: it reorders below P0 here (a substrate/judge effect; above P0 on the 3-judge 90q panel). Ragged p5/p6 lack a valid shared substrate and remain descriptive only (see ragged_descriptive).

run_noise_robustness.interpretation: For EVERY full-coverage member, single-run and replicate-averaged resampling agree on (i) the sign of the gap vs P0 and (ii) the Holm separation verdict. Replicate-averaging does not reorder the members relative to P0, so the single-run ranking is NOT a run-noise artefact. This directly refutes 'you rank on single runs but run-noise dominates'.

top_performers_claim.note: Load-bearing headline claim: the top-3 full-coverage cluster members {p1,p4,p7} EACH Holm-significantly separate above P0, under BOTH single-run and replicate-averaged resampling on the shared 30q substrate. This is the claim the headline rests on and it holds.

p8_substrate_disclosure.note: p8 is a LEGITIMATE full-panel cluster member (rank-5, ABOVE P0, on the canonical 3-judge 90q headline panel; see headline.rank_desc). On this GPT-5.2-ONLY 30-query replicate subset it reorders BELOW P0 in BOTH single-run and replicate-averaged resampling. Because run-averaging does NOT move it (single-run agrees with replicate-avg on p8<P0), its below-P0 position is a SUBSTRATE/JUDGE effect (single judge, 30 queries), NOT run-noise. p8 is disclosed here in full and is NOT dropped from the family.

separation.note: Replicate-averaged member-vs-P0 records for ALL full-coverage members (incl p8). 'all_members_above_p0' is FALSE because p8 reorders below P0 on this substrate; that is expected and disclosed (p8_substrate_disclosure) and is NOT the survives verdict.

tie.power_note: tie tested on 30 q (headline used 90 q): paired-diff CIs ~1.7x wider, so +/-0.05 equivalence is mechanically harder to declare. Max within-cluster |diff| is 0.1481. The tie now spans the full member set incl p8, which the panel places above P0 but this substrate places below, so a within-band tie is NOT expected here; treat as UNDERPOWERED/substrate-shifted, not an ordering.

ragged_descriptive.note: p5/p6 have ragged judged-replicate coverage on the shared substrate (p8 now has FULL 3-replicate coverage and is handled in clean_substrate, incl its substrate disclosure). The pairwise blocks below use each pair's OWN intersection, so they are NOT on a shared substrate and CANNOT carry the survives verdict; the clean_substrate run-noise-robustness block does.

headline_replicated.followup: Patterns p2,p3,p9,p11,p12 have NO judged replicate runs (single judged run only); p5,p6 still have RAGGED replicate coverage (<30 common q) on the shared substrate. The follow-up is to judge the EXISTING on-disk replicate report runs under checkpoints/<pattern>/<timestamp>/ with GPT-5.2 so the full ranking — not just the run-noise-robustness and tie claims — can be re-ranked replicate-averaged.

human_anchor_summary._note: human_anchor_summary — AGGREGATION ONLY (no recompute) of the already-landed judge_vs_human (panel-vs-expert agreement on the public human-label sets) and judge_vs_gold (panel factual AUC vs mechanical verifiable-answer gold + the cross-family DeLong) into one headline table answering 'are the rubric scores anchored to human / verifiable ground truth, and which judge is most aligned?'. Every number is copied verbatim from those two sibling keys; status flags are carried through unmodified.

judge_vs_gold_factual.note: no judge-vs-gold factual AUC arm for this family

cross_family_factual_delong.finding: On the MATCHED common report set (n=259 reports scored by all panel judges), GPT-5.2's factual verdicts are answer-sensitive (common-set AUC 0.6483) while both Claude judges are near-chance. The cross-family AUC gap is now backed by a paired DeLong test on the SAME reports (it previously compared different per-judge report sets, untested): gpt52>opus diff=0.107 (DeLong p=0.031337), gpt52>sonnet diff=0.1566 (DeLong p=0.000275); both significant at .05, sonnet also significant under the conservative paired cluster bootstrap. The answer signal reflects general report completeness, not factual-dimension specificity; the load-bearing result is the cross-family validity asymmetry, now matched-set and difference-tested.

caveats.draco_full_excluded: draco_full is EXCLUDED for label leakage (human_label == criterion target-polarity, a constant per criterion, NOT a per-report human grade); its 'agreement' would measure polarity detection, not report-grading agreement, so it is not counted here.
caveats.awaiting_panel_or_pending: Cells with status 'awaiting_panel' / 'pending_judge' are sets our 9-dim panel has not yet scored for that family; the wiring slots them in with no code change once verdicts land. They are surfaced, not dropped.

small_n.deepfactbench: small-n: only 15 report clusters (621 claims nested in 15 reports)
small_n.drb_race: small-n: 50 annotated tasks (per-dimension cells nested in 50 tasks)

caveats.no_local_gold_arm: judge_vs_gold has no 'local' factual-AUC arm (the 7B judge was not run on the verifiable-answer slice); that cell is marked not_evaluated.
caveats.gold_signal_is_general: The verifiable-answer signal reflects GENERAL report completeness, not factual-dimension specificity; the load-bearing gold result is the cross-family validity ASYMMETRY, not an absolute factual certification.

anchoring_provenance.note: n_human_labelled_items_anchored sums the joined item counts of every SCORED (family × valid human set) agreement cell; n_verifiable_gold_reports is the judge_vs_gold factual-AUC report count (gpt52).

most_aligned_judge.evidence: GPT-5.2 is the only panel judge whose verifiable-gold factual AUC excludes chance (AUC 0.6587; correct-minus-incorrect delta CI excludes 0), and the matched-set DeLong test puts it significantly above both Claude judges on the same reports; on the human-label sets the GPT-5.2 family also leads on DRB-RACE Spearman and HealthBench AUC where it is scored.

human_anchor_summary.anchoring_statement: Our rubric scores are anchored to ground truth on two independent axes: agreement with EXPERT HUMAN labels across 7 scored (judge-family × public-human-set) cells totalling 5,765 human-labelled items (DRB-RACE expert RACE labels, ExpertQA, DeepFactBench, HealthBench; DRACO-full excluded for label leakage), and agreement with 322 MECHANICALLY verifiable-answer gold reports (LitQA2 + DeepSearchQA). GPT-5.2 is the most human- and gold-aligned judge: it is the only panel judge whose verifiable-gold factual AUC excludes chance (0.66) and it is significantly above both Claude judges on the matched report set by a paired DeLong test.

citation_url_verification._purpose: Empirical rebuttal to the 'LLM judges reward citation FORM over substance; 3-13% of cited URLs are fabricated' critique (arXiv:2604.03173-style). Two channels: (1) HTTP resolution of a stratified sample of cited URLs measures the actual dead/fabricated rate; (2) claim-level entailment of the cited subset measures SUPPORT (substance). Numbers are MEASURED here, not imported.
citation_url_verification.coverage_note: URL channel: 399 URLs resolved out of 10215 unique resolvable URLs (22903 total citation slots; 6803 are non-resolvable web-search-synthesis/placeholder slots). SUPPORT channel coverage is LIMITED: only 176 citation slots carry a claim-level entailment verdict (C0 sampled claims per report; few sampled claims bore an inline [n] marker), so the support rate is over n=176 cited claims, NOT the full corpus. Both rates are reported on their own measured base; neither is extrapolated, and no external fabrication % is asserted as confirmed.

url_resolution_channel.sampling: stratified across 12 patterns; seed=7; unique URLs only
url_resolution_channel.resolver_notes: HEAD then GET fallback; follow redirects; timeout=5.0s; per-host min gap=1.0s; verify=True. 2xx/3xx and 401/403/405/406/429/451 (access-restricted) and TLS handshake errors are counted RESOLVE-LIVE (host exists & answered / is reachable); 404/410 and DNS/connection failures are DEAD/fabricated; timeouts and other exceptions are INDETERMINATE and excluded from the determinate dead rate.

entailment_support_channel.method: C0/FActScore claim-level entailment (df_c0_verdicts.parquet); same pipeline behind canonical['citation_faithfulness'] and e14 oracle entailment. Cited subset = claims with non-null citation_idx.

citation_url_verification.interpretation: If the measured dead/fabricated rate is in the same low band the critique cites (single-digit %) the corpus is NOT pathologically fabricated; and if the SUPPORT rate of cited claims is materially above zero, citations carry substance, not just form. Conversely a LOW support rate would CONCEDE the substance critique while still showing URLs mostly resolve -- the honest framing the paper should adopt. Read both channels together.

compute_ledger.note: Per-architecture compute ledger supporting the matched-compute claim. compute_multiple_vs_p0 gives, per metric, how many times the single-call P0 baseline's compute each pipeline spends. PRIMARY ledger (per_pattern) is query-aligned (n<=90) from checkpoints/experiments/base_p{N}/ and reproduces the canonical mean_cost_proxy_usd exactly. GPT-4o runs are on PTU (no per-token bill, total_cost_usd=0), so cost_usd is a token*$5/M proxy; local 7B (p9,p10) use elapsed*$1e-4/s, hence report BOTH token and cost multiples. gen_tokens_mean is null: the canonical checkpoints record only total_tokens, with NO prompt/completion/generation split, and the trace tool_calls reconcile to only a fraction of total tokens, so no honest generation-token figure is derivable. process_detail_unaligned (n_LLM_calls / n_searches / n_urls) comes ONLY from raw traces that are NOT aligned to the canonical 90 query_ids, have uneven coverage (30..848 traces/pattern) and some 0-valued fields; treat as indicative process shape, not query-matched means. This makes concrete that the bounded quality gain across the GPT-4o cluster coincides with a large (multi-fold) compute increase over P0, consistent with the disentanglement clamp result that much of the gain is a compute artefact rather than an architecture effect.

search_robustness._purpose: Reviewer-critical robustness check: tests whether the orchestration gain (cluster of pipelines ranked above the single-call P0 baseline) is partly an artefact of DIFFERENTIAL SEARCH FAILURE rather than architecture, by conditioning the cluster-vs-P0 score gap on per-arm search success.

cluster_definition.rule: patterns ranked above base_p0 in headline.rank_desc

data_sources.search_volume_success: checkpoints/<pattern>/<ts>/trace.json -> tool_calls over RETRIEVAL_VERBS {search,academic_search,widen,deepen,extract,frozen_corpus}: attempts = #calls, docs = sum(n_results), yield = docs/attempt (HARMONISED, architecture-comparable; a 429/timeout/empty fetch -> n_results=0). Raw n_search_queries / n_unique_urls_visited also kept but flagged NON-comparable (verb-name-specific). Traced subset of canonical qids; dedup latest ts.
data_sources.ledger_null_note: compute_ledger.per_pattern carries NO n_searches (query-aligned manifests log only tokens/cost/sections/citations); search volume recovered from traces.

score_vs_searchvolume_corr.covariate: mean retrieval ATTEMPTS per arm (harmonised external-fetch calls)

covariates: resolve_rate (1 - dead/fabricated URL rate, full audit)

cluster_gap_conditioned_on_search.interpretation: is_cluster coefficient = architecture gap holding per-arm retrieval yield (docs/attempt) constant. survives=True means the orchestration gain is NOT explained away by search success.

search_failure_differential_detail.interpretation: failure_differential=True only if the true-failure signal (dead/fabricated-URL rate) BOTH varies materially AND is score-linked IN THE CONFOUNDING DIRECTION (cluster arms failing LESS, i.e. corr(resolve,score)>0 and cluster dead-rate < non-cluster). Here the dead-rate spread is small (0.0-0.088) AND the direction is ANTI-confounding: corr(resolve_rate, score) is NEGATIVE, and the cluster's mean dead rate is NOT lower than P0's group, so differential search failure cannot be the engine of the cluster-vs-P0 gain. The docs/attempt spread is large but reflects deliberate fan-out DESIGN, not failure, and its score correlation is weak/the wrong sign to explain the gain.
search_failure_differential_detail.attribution_caveat: Per-arm 429/timeout/s2_error COUNTS are NOT attributable from trace.json (it logs tool_calls + their n_results, not provider error codes) and the run logs interleave patterns, so raw 429 counts cannot be cleanly split per arm and are NOT claimed. Measurable failure signals: (i) docs/attempt yield from traces (a 429/timeout/empty fetch -> n_results=0), (ii) dead/fabricated-URL rate from the full citation-URL audit. The dead-rate spread is 0.0-0.088 across all arms — uniformly low.

search_robustness.verdict: Orchestration gain SURVIVES conditioning on per-arm search success; true search failure (dead/fabricated-URL rate) is ROUGHLY_UNIFORM across architectures. The cluster-vs-P0 advantage is NOT an artefact of differential search failure: (1) the is_cluster coefficient stays positive and its 95% CI excludes 0 after controlling for harmonised retrieval yield, at BOTH arm level (coef=0.2664, ci=[0.1352, 0.3976]) and per-query (coef=0.1813, ci=[0.1517, 0.2109]); (2) dead/fabricated-URL rate is uniformly low (0.0-0.0882) across all arms, and the cluster's mean dead rate is if anything marginally HIGHER than the non-cluster group (+0.0085), i.e. search failure runs the WRONG way to manufacture the gain; (3) retrieval VOLUME/yield, where it differs, is NEGATIVELY correlated with score (higher-volume arms score no better), the opposite of a search-success confound. DATA CAVEAT: search-volume/yield measured on a TRACED SUBSET (~30 of 90 canonical queries for most pipelines; p0=43, p9=83; p11/p12 have no usable traces); resolve/dead rates from the full 90-query URL audit. The raw n_search_queries / n_unique_urls trace fields are NOT architecture-comparable (verb-name-specific: p5 logs 0 'searches', p1 logs 0 urls) so a HARMONISED docs/attempt yield is used as the covariate. Per-arm 429/timeout counts are not attributable from disk.

per_query_clustered_inference._note: Cluster-correct inference for per_query_robustness (Moulton problem: is_cluster varies only across the 11 arms, so the landed plain-OLS SE 0.0181 / CI [0.1547, 0.2256] over n=399 rows is anticonservative). Rows rebuilt with the machinery of scripts/build_search_robustness.py and identity-checked against the landed coef/n. G=11 clusters (arms). The plain-OLS per-query CI should be read as DESCRIPTIVE; cluster-level inference here is the citable interval. Deterministic: Rademacher wild bootstrap fully enumerated (2^11=2048); Webb seeded.

wild_cluster_bootstrap._ci_note: test_inversion_ci95 is the recommended wild-cluster CI (MacKinnon-Webb): the set of beta0 not rejected by the null-imposed studentised test at 5%. The unrestricted percentile-t interval is a cruder construction, reported as sensitivity.

arm_level_t_ci_restated._note: landed arm-level CI [0.1647, 0.3605] used 1.96 with dof=8; t(8) CI here

per_query_clustered_inference.verdict: is_cluster coef +0.1813: CR1 CI [0.0338, 0.3288] (t(10)), CR2/Bell-McCaffrey CI [-0.0321, 0.3947] (df_BM=4.9), wild-cluster (null-imposed, Rademacher enumerated) p = 0.0107, Webb p = 0.0116, test-inversion wild CI [0.0255, 0.3258]. Cluster-correct constructions do NOT all reject zero: DEMOTE the per-query result to descriptive and lean on the arm-level regression (t(8) CI [0.1352, 0.3976]) only.

contrast_a_bounded_gain.definition: mean(p4_base) - mean(p0_base), paired over base subset

contrast_b_oracle_bottleneck.definition: mean(p4_oracle) - mean(p4_base), paired over matched oracle subset

coverage.note: 20 heaviest queries skipped at the 1800s gpt-4.1 per-query timeout; findings computed on the completed subset (paired contrasts drop any query missing from an arm, so both arms are matched).

second_backbone_gpt41.interpretation: Qualitative replication HOLDS on gpt-4.1: the orchestration gain is bounded (0.086, 95% CI excludes 0) AND the oracle adds a significant lift (0.079, 95% CI excludes 0). The strict 'oracle dominates orchestration' ordering is a TIE here (0.079 vs 0.086, ~equal) rather than db>da. Coverage 100/120: the 20 heaviest queries hit the 1800s gpt-4.1 per-query timeout; paired contrasts drop them from BOTH arms (a generalisability caveat on the heaviest queries, not a within-contrast confound).

e11_vtr._note: E11 verify-then-refine (VTR): per-base-pipeline overall-score lift of a guided self-verify-and-refine pass OVER ITS MATCHED-BUDGET UNGUIDED-REVISION CONTROL, on the matched query set, judged by GPT-5.2 (judge-independent of the GPT-4o pipelines under test). Paired per query: Wilcoxon signed-rank + per-query paired bootstrap CI. Both P0 and P4 lifts are significant (p<0.01).
e11_vtr.contrast: vtr_arm minus control_arm (unguided-revision control at matched budget)

e6_decontamination._note: E6 decontamination robustness on the paper headline. A regex+classifier detector over each report's CITATION and SEARCH snippets flags contamination (metadata-host + question-context buckets); the flagged queries are DROPPED and the headline recomputed. Headline SURVIVES: after dropping the contaminated queries the top orchestration cluster is STILL flat and the orchestration lift over P0 (cluster_minus_p0) is unchanged in sign and roughly in size (in fact LARGER). Rank-1 shifts P1->P5 on the tiny 17-query residual (expected n=17 sampling noise; P1/P4/P5 all inside the flat top band) — reported, not the survival criterion. Recomputed source: results/contamination_e6/decontaminated_headline.json (prereg E6).
e6_decontamination.method: regex+classifier over citations/search snippets (metadata_host + question_context buckets)

survive_detail.rank1_shift_note: rank-1 shift on the 17-query residual is expected sampling noise and is NOT the survival criterion; the flat top cluster + positive cluster_minus_p0 are.

judge_scale_standardized_gaps._note: Reviewer-objection control for the 0.146-panel vs 0.065-GPT-5.2 P0-to-cluster gap claim: raw per-judge gaps conflate judge scale with judge bias. Per judge we report the paired Cohen's d over queries (gap / SD of paired per-query cluster-P0 diffs) and the within-judge z-scored gap (gap / SD of that judge's scores over all base-pattern cells; z-scoring is linear so this equals the gap recomputed on z-scored scores). Sonnet corrected via overall_score_recomputed. Cluster = six-pattern top cluster {p1,p4,p5,p6,p7,p8}, cluster_q = per-judge mean over available cluster patterns, paired by query with P0. delta_* vs gpt52 use a SHARED seeded query-bootstrap (same draws for all judges -> paired CIs on the difference).

clean_residual_capability._note: Frontier-vs-7B capability gaps recomputed on the E6 contamination-clean residual (the 17 queries the citation-basis detector does NOT flag), extending the e6_decontamination control from the orchestration contrast to finding (ii). Three-judge panel mean per query (sonnet corrected), paired by query with P9; cluster = six-pattern top cluster {p1,p4,p5,p6,p7,p8}. Full-90 references recomputed on the identical basis. gpt52_only = family-clean single-judge sensitivity. Seeded query bootstrap, percentile CIs.

headline_cluster_gap._note: Canonical backing for the paper's previously-unbacked headline gap numbers: the six-pattern orchestrated-cluster mean (P1,P4,P5,P6,P7,P8) minus the single-pass baseline P0, on the three-judge panel mean (quoted as 0.145/0.146) and on the family-clean GPT-5.2 judge alone (quoted as 0.065), plus the P0-vs-P9 and cluster-vs-P9 companions. Recomputed from the released parquets and verified to reproduce the store's own headline / single_judge_gpt52 means. CIs are query-clustered (resample the 90 query ids) paired bootstrap percentile intervals.

three_judge.basis: mean-of-pattern-means, available-case: each pattern's score is its pooled judge-cell mean over all available (query x judge) cells of the three-judge panel {gpt52, claude_opus, claude_sonnet}, with claude_sonnet's corrupted overall_score replaced by overall_score_recomputed (identical to the store's headline.per_pattern.mean_3judge, n_cells 265-270 per pattern); the cluster value is the UNWEIGHTED mean of the six cluster patterns' means (each pattern weighted equally, not each cell/query).

gpt52.basis: mean-of-pattern-means over the GPT-5.2 judge alone (identical to the store's single_judge_gpt52.per_pattern.mean; n=87-90 queries per pattern); cluster = unweighted mean of the six cluster patterns' means.

length_adjusted_headline._note: Length-control reanalysis of the HEADLINE contrasts, applying the paper's own frozen_vintage length adjustment (pooled OLS: score ~ pattern dummies + beta*(words/1000 - grand mean); each dummy = counterfactual score at grand-mean length) to the main 11-pattern x 90-query three-judge run. The orchestrated cluster produces systematically longer reports (~1.9k words vs P0 ~1.2k, P9 ~0.7k), so the raw headline gaps are partially a verbosity artefact under judges with a positive length slope. Spec B adds query fixed effects (controls query-difficulty confounding of the within-pattern slope); spec C uses log-words (the judge-bias audit's scale). All gaps are on the mean-of-pattern-means basis of 'headline_cluster_gap'.

data.length_unit: report_word_count from df_runs.parquet (whitespace word count of the released .md; tokenizer-independent, same unit as frozen_vintage); every judged cell has a non-null word count

pooled_ols_kwords_vintage_method.method: cell-level pooled OLS over all 11 arms x 3 judges: score ~ 11 pattern dummies (no intercept) + beta*(words/1000 - grand-mean kwords); identical to frozen_vintage.length_control (whose slope was +0.1748)

query_fixed_effects_kwords.method: spec A + query fixed effects (within-query demeaning, Frisch-Waugh; P0 reference, so coefficients are adjusted gaps vs P0; bootstrap gives each resampled query COPY its own FE). Controls query-difficulty confounding of the within-pattern length-score slope.

pooled_ols_log_words.method: spec A with log(words) (clipped at 1) instead of linear kwords - the judge-bias audit's scale, where beta(log wc) ~ 0.04-0.11; arms evaluated at the grand-mean of log-words

min_100_words_filter.note: spec A on cells with report >= 100 words (drops the degenerate near-empty short tail concentrated in P0/P9), point estimates only

judge_fe_check.note: spec A + centred judge dummies (adjusted means at balanced judge mix; guards the slight judge-coverage imbalance), point only

bootstrap.note: np.random.default_rng(seed); the SAME resampled query-id block feeds every spec and judge each iteration (paired); percentile CIs; two-sided p = 2*min(P(d>0),P(d<0)) floored at 1/n_boot.

interpretation_caveats: With pattern dummies the pooled length slope is identified from WITHIN-pattern variation, which conflates judge length-preference with query-level material richness (successful retrieval yields both longer reports and better scores); it is therefore an UPPER-bound-ish verbosity correction. Spec B (query FE) removes the query side and is the preferred causal-ish spec; spec C matches the judge-bias audit's log scale.

Grand-mean evaluation (~1,600 words) sits at the edge of P9's length support (mean 726, p95 ~1,622): P9's adjusted mean involves mild extrapolation, so length-adjusted P0-vs-P9 / cluster-vs-P9 gaps carry more model dependence than the cluster-vs-P0 gap.
P0 and P9 have a short tail of degenerate near-empty reports; see sensitivity_points.min_100_words_filter.

verdict.summary: Raw three-judge cluster-vs-P0 gap 0.145 -> -0.003 under the paper's own vintage-method length adjustment (slope 0.228/kword), 0.025 with query FE (slope 0.184), 0.049 with log-words. P0-vs-P9 shrinks 0.231 -> 0.113 (vintage) but stays positive in all specs; cluster-vs-P9 0.376 -> 0.11 likewise.

lr_pattern_x_source_refit._note: Audit + refit of carried_metrics.lr_pattern_x_source ('202.3, df 44'). contamination_precision_audit._note: A3 contamination-detector PRECISION AUDIT. Rule-based, deterministic review of the CONCRETE trigger of every one of the E6 73/90 contamination flags (regex bucket + host + URL + frozen GPT-4o classifier label). Query category = max severity over its flagged public snippets: TRUE (benchmark's own content leaked -- explicit_answer_leak, a benchmark NAME token in a flagged URL, or a classifier question/answer reproduction), AMBIGUOUS (generic Q&A/answer/solutions surface, benchmark-source-host metadata hit, or a classifier metadata_leak), BENIGN (metadata_host on a generic academic-registry host only -- an ordinary scientific citation). Conservative toward the detector: any classifier-asserted question/answer reproduction counts TRUE and the ambiguous bucket is offered as an upper bound. Sensitivity recompute reuses the EXACT contamination.clean_residual_capability conventions (3-judge panel, sonnet corrected, paired-by-query with P9, six-pattern cluster, seed 20260702, 5000 boot); the clean-17 point gaps reproduce that landed key exactly (asserted).

detector_mechanics.note: Union is entirely regex-driven at query level (classifier adds 0 queries); the GPT-4o reader confirmed 0 of the 1021 regex-flagged public snippets (regex/classifier public overlap = 0); no flagged URL carries a benchmark name token and explicit_answer_leak never fires -> the gate reduces to 'cited >=1 academic-registry host'.

crosscheck_e6_decontamination_cluster_mi.note: E6 uses a 5-pattern cluster {p1,p4,p6,p7,p8} with an unpaired panel-mean-over-patterns basis; this audit uses the 6-pattern clean_residual_capability basis (paired per-query, cluster incl. p5) -> values are close in sign and size, not identical.

contamination_precision_audit.paper_ready_statement: Manual, rule-based review of the concrete trigger behind each of the 73 contamination flags finds the detector is dominated by false positives: 57 (78%) fire only on an ordinary citation to a generic academic-registry host (813 of 1021 flags are arXiv.org, and GPT-4o -- reading the content -- confirms none of them), 13 are ambiguous generic Q&A/answer surfaces, and only 3 carry concrete evidence of benchmark leakage (all three classifier-identified near-duplicate deepsearch_qa questions, no answer leak). Estimated precision is 4% (95% CI 1-12%), rising to at most 22% if every ambiguous flag is counted as true. Rebuilding the clean set as the 17 never-flagged queries plus the 57 benign-flagged queries (n=74) leaves all three headline effects intact -- orchestration lift cluster-minus-P0 = 0.1456 (95% CI [0.1064, 0.1888]), capability gap P0-minus-P9 = 0.2114, cluster-minus-P9 = 0.357, all excluding zero -- confirming the E6 17-query residual is conservative-by-construction rather than the effect being an artefact of the queries that survived flagging.

irt_tensor.method_note: Many-Facet Rasch / IRT fit to the binary judged-verdict tensor. Facets: report-ability theta_r (report = pattern x query, R=985), criterion-difficulty b_c (item = md5-hashed criterion text, C=673; identical rubric text collapses to one item so general criteria anchor across queries), judge-severity s_j (J=3). 1PL/MFRM logit P(satisfied)=theta_r - b_c - s_j; 2PL adds criterion discrimination a_c (logit=a_c*(theta_r-b_c-s_j)). Estimator: penalised joint MLE (MAP) via L-BFGS-B with analytic sparse gradients; weak Gaussian priors (SD_theta=SD_b=5.0, SD_logA=0.5) control JML separation, judges near-unregularised (SD_s=100.0). Identification: criteria & judge severities centred to mean 0, offset folded into theta; 2PL geometric-mean discrimination free (shrunk to 1 by prior). Sign: higher b_c and higher s_j => harder to satisfy (severe). Filter: satisfied_is_known, 11 base patterns base_p0..base_p10, 3 core judges (gpt52, claude_opus, claude_sonnet); 115 empty-text criteria dropped. Pure CPU, no API calls.
irt_tensor.per_dimension_difficulty_note: PRIMARY per_dimension_difficulty = mean 1PL criterion difficulty b_c (logits, higher=harder) over WELL-OBSERVED criteria (n>=30 verdicts: the general DRACO rubric statements shared across queries, the only identifiable items). The all-item unweighted mean is corrupted because ~84% of criteria are query-specific singletons with prior-dominated b_c; the verdict-weighted mean is provided too and agrees with well-observed. PREDICTION test: factual_accuracy & information_recall highest; analytical_depth lowest.
irt_tensor.judge_severity_note: 1PL s_j in logits, centred to mean 0; higher = more severe (satisfies less).
irt_tensor.var_ratio_note: per-judge report abilities re-fit with criterion difficulties anchored at joint 1PL b_c. Var(severity)=variance of the 3 judge mean-ability levels; Var(interaction)=variance of judge x report residual after removing judge level & report consensus. Raw interaction variance is inflated by per-report estimation noise (~38 verdicts/report/judge); disattenuated version subtracts the (2/3)*mean(SE^2) noise floor. Both severity and interaction reported so the paper can state levels-vs-orderings honestly.

irt_n_eff_or_separation_reliability.note: effective_judge_count = k/(1+(k-1)*rbar) over mean inter-judge report-ability correlation (k=3); an IRT-ability analog to the canonical agreement-based n_eff=1.655. report/judge separation reliability = (Var(hat)-mean SE^2)/Var(hat).

low_discrimination_criteria.text: Different sections draw from different sources rather than relying on a single source

irt_tensor.low_discrimination_criteria_note: 2PL a_c < 0.30 among items with >=100 verdicts (well-estimated). Near-zero a_c = criterion does not separate reports (near-constant pass/fail) -> pruning candidate.

isoquant._note: Capability x architecture isoquant, all rungs judged by GPT-5.2 (gpt52). Capability axis (7B<8B<14B<gpt-4o<gpt-4.1) is measured at the SIMPLEST architecture (P9 local scaffold = P0-equivalent); local rungs use length-adjusted scores (within-frozen-pool OLS, strips the verbosity confound) and frozen retrieval (gpt-4o extractor held constant); frontier rungs use raw gpt52 with live retrieval. Architecture axis (P0->P4, cost 1x->17.5x) is measured at gpt-4o and gpt-4.1. The full 2D surface is UNDER-IDENTIFIED (no P4-on-local cell); what is estimable is the two margins plus the P0/P4 contrast at two frontier tiers (the interaction slice).

capability_ladder_at_P0_architecture.note: newer vintage than 7B/14B -> off the pure-capacity line (vintage confound)

at_gpt4_1.p0_note: Corrected 2026-07-28 (adversarial review round 16): this p0 field must be the mean over the SAME 32 paired queries as p4/paired_delta_p4_minus_p0, not the 45-query full gpt-4.1 P0 sample (0.4870333, which is capability_ladder_at_P0_architecture gpt-4.1 tier q_raw). Verified by direct recomputation from results/judge_gpt52_gpt41_backbone/{p0_base,p4_base}: paired_delta (0.0861) was already correct (computed from the right 32-query pairing); only this p0 companion field was stale.

frontier_separability.verdict: Architecture premium is essentially CONSTANT across the two frontier tiers (0.082 vs 0.086; interaction +0.0041, tiny vs CIs) -> additively separable / smooth isoquant over gpt-4o<->gpt-4.1: architecture and capability act as SUBSTITUTES here, no detectable complementarity. Complementarity at the low-capability end is UNTESTED (no P4-on-local cell).

headline_isoquant_cell.readout: DIRECTLY OBSERVED (no extrapolation): P4-on-gpt-4o (0.467) ~= P0-on-gpt-4.1 (0.487) -- roughly on the SAME isoquant. One base-model generation upgrade (gpt-4o->gpt-4.1) delivers ~+0.103 quality at P0, which equals-or-exceeds the entire P0->P4 orchestration stack (+0.082) at ~1/17 the compute. Along the frontier segment, capability is the cheaper axis and substitutes for architecture.

exchange_rate.statement: One architecture step (P0->P4, ~0.082 quality) buys about 3.2 parameter-doublings on the local ladder (~8x params) OR ~3.8 small-model vintage-steps (~2 years of local-model progress) -- but this is a WITHIN-LOCAL extrapolation of a small, near-zero-touching slope (ratio CI is wide, ~2-15 doublings) and the capability axis is markedly non-uniform, so quote as an order of magnitude.

compute_confound_caveat.note: The P0->P4 premium (0.082) is an UPPER BOUND on the pure-architecture effect: a matched-budget probe (on P1) attributes a borderline ~40% of the P1>P0 gap to raw compute (not significant, Wilcoxon p=0.053). If a similar share holds for P4, the architecture-only premium is nearer ~0.05, shrinking every exchange rate above by ~40%.

coverage_notes: Full 2D response surface NOT fittable: no P4-on-local cell, so architecture-only OLS is L-shaped (arch varies only at gpt-4o & gpt-4.1; capability varies only at P0). Interaction estimable ONLY between gpt-4o and gpt-4.1.

Retrieval-control discontinuity: local rungs use FROZEN retrieval (gpt-4o extractor held constant, isolates the generation model); frontier rungs use LIVE retrieval. The ladder stitches two experiments.
Query-set / n mismatch: local rungs = 89 frozen queries; gpt-4o P0 = 90 live; gpt-4.1 P0 = 45-query subset (20 heaviest queries timed out at 1800s).

Capability 'tier' is NOT a uniform unit: local steps are small (+0.01 to +0.02) but the 14B->gpt-4o jump (+0.07) and gpt-4o->gpt-4.1 jump (+0.10) are large -- a regime change at the local->frontier boundary.
8B (Qwen3-8B) is a newer vintage than the 7B/14B Qwen2.5 pair, so the pure-capacity slope uses only the same-vintage 7B->14B pair (canonical 0.0253/doubling).
isoquant.verdict: ESTIMABLE (partial). The isoquant is smooth/separable and capability-favouring over the FRONTIER segment: one gpt-4o->gpt-4.1 generation (~+0.10) >= the full P0->P4 stack (~+0.08) at 1/17 the compute, and P4@gpt-4o ~= P0@gpt-4.1 sit on one isoquant. Exchange rate ~ 1 architecture step ~= 3 param-doublings (order of magnitude). Complementarity at low capability is plausible but UNMEASURED -- the ladder is too thin (missing P4-on-local) to fit a clean interacted surface across the whole range.

oracle_claim_type._note: Claim-type stratification of the oracle factual channel. Oracle condition = perfect/gold retrieval (df_e14_oracle_verdicts); base condition = live retrieval (df_c0_verdicts). VFA = fraction of claims with verdict=='supports' (matches df_*_per_report.verified_factual_accuracy = n_supports/n_claims). Claims are tagged by simple text heuristics (regex below). PRIMARY analysis is matched on the 11 queries and 8 patterns shared by both conditions, pooled over patterns, with a QUERY cluster bootstrap (seed 20260703, 10000 reps). The oracle/base reports are different generations so claims are NOT paired claim-by-claim -- this is a between-report VFA contrast at the claim-type level.
oracle_claim_type.verdict_to_vfa: VFA(type) = mean(verdict=='supports') over claims of that type

typing_heuristics.multihop_causal: \b(because|therefore|thus|hence|due to|leads? to|results? in|resulting|caused? by|enabl|allow|drives?|contribut|as a result)\b
typing_heuristics.caveat: Heuristics are noisy; multi-hop is under-detected (citation_idx is null for ~85% of claims, near-zero inline [n] markers) so multi-hop rests on causal connectives only and is low-power.

aggregate_matched.note: Modest positive aggregate (consistent with e14 cluster retrieval_component 0.092 and the flat e5 dose slope) -- the stratification asks WHERE this small lift lives.

coverage_notes: Only 11 queries overlap between the oracle and base conditions (oracle uses a hash/dsqa query sample, base c0 uses the variance-stratified UUID+hash sample); the QUERY cluster bootstrap resamples these 11, so matched CIs are WIDE. Unmatched (all-query) robustness is reported alongside.
multihop cell is tiny (matched n=46 oracle / 25 base) -> its delta is directional only; rely on the 2-way synthesis bucket (comparative+multihop) for the powered synthesis test.

The prediction (single-hop improves; numeric/aggregative/multi-hop carry the flatness) is PARTIALLY refined by the data: the flatness is concentrated in COMPARATIVE-AGGREGATIVE claims; NUMERIC claims behave like grounding and improve the MOST.
Base numeric VFA is very low (~0.10): without gold evidence the model's numbers rarely verify against retrieved sources; oracle grounding is exactly what a specific-number lookup needs.
oracle_claim_type.verdict: SUPPORTED WITH A TWIST. The modest aggregate oracle lift (matched +0.079) is NOT uniform across claim types. GROUNDING claims improve (grounding delta +0.115: single-hop +0.087, numeric +0.230) while SYNTHESIS claims stay flat (synthesis delta -0.004), driven by comparative-aggregative claims (-0.013). So perfect evidence buys GROUNDING (look up a fact/number) but not SYNTHESIS PROPER (compare/aggregate across sources) -- the flat aggregate hides a real grounding gain masked by a flat comparative-aggregative channel. Refines the preregistered guess: it is comparative-aggregative, not numeric, that carries the flatness. Small-n (11 shared queries) -> directional; unmatched robustness agrees on the ordering.

_meta.title: Synthesis-as-binding-constraint: four cross-field imports + closed-form winner's curse
_meta.substrate: gpt52 single-judge unless noted; pure CPU on df_*.parquet + canonical_numbers.json

evt.cross_field_import: Extreme-value theory / winner's curse (Gumbel/BLUE order statistics)
evt.caveats: sigma_run is the gpt52 single-judge run SD (matched to routability.raw single-judge substrate). The Gumbel/exact closed form is E[max]-mean under the EXCHANGEABLE null (all 11 arms equal true quality); it is an UPPER bound on the winner's curse and does NOT credit genuine arch x query signal. The data-driven bootstrap (which keeps real signal) attributes 24.7%% to noise; the closed form shows the SCALE of the winner's-curse risk is comparable to the whole raw effect. The 3-judge panel headroom (0.0561) is even smaller, consistent with a less noisy substrate.
evt.verdict: Pure per-query run-selection noise (sigma_run=0.0591, N=11) manufactures a Gumbel E[max]-mean headroom of 0.0834 (exact order-stat 0.0937), i.e. 88%-99% of the raw oracle headroom (0.0945). The raw oracle 'routability' number is on the same scale as a pure selection artefact; the winner's-curse-corrected bootstrap keeps 75% (0.0712), and the realisable router still fails to beat best-fixed.

oring.cross_field_import: Kremer (1993) O-ring production function (multiplicative stage complementarity)
oring.binding_constraint_after_intervention: utilisation / synthesis-of-sources (retrieval-availability falsified by E5 gold injection; E14 utilisation ceiling 0.32). The low retrieval-labelled stage is a downstream synthesis (grounding/recall) bottleneck, not a source-availability one.
oring.passive_fit_caveat: Y=overall_score is a weighted SUM of the nine dimensions, so the additive model has a mechanical advantage and the interaction coefficients are ~0 by construction. The passive fit therefore CANNOT falsify O-ring complementarity; use the intervention test.

oring_intervention_prediction.note: Both PASSIVE-fit models extrapolate a large gain from perfect retrieval (additive 0.346, multiplicative fitted 0.129) because they are confounded by Y being a weighted sum. The CAUSAL intervention (E5) shows ~0 factual gain and E14 caps utilisation at 0.32: perfect retrieval does not rescue quality because source-utilisation (a synthesis capability) is binding. The gap between the passive prediction and the null intervention IS the O-ring result.

oring.verdict: REFINED (honest): the NOMINAL min stage is retrieval=0.319 (synthesis=0.543, citation=0.411), driven by low information_recall (0.179) and factual_accuracy (0.300). But the O-ring INTERVENTION falsifies retrieval-AVAILABILITY as the binding input: injecting perfect retrieval (E5 gold q_ret->1) gives a factual slope of -0.0011 (CI [-0.03500797211962474, 0.03278574989740243] includes 0), a g100-g000 factual change of -0.0028, and E14 caps source-utilisation at 0.32<<1 with only 0.092 of the factual channel attributable to retrieval availability. So the low retrieval-stage score is a UTILISATION (synthesis-of-sources) bottleneck, not a retrieval-availability one. Raising the nominal min stage's INPUT yields ~0 gain because the binding factor is the downstream synthesis/utilisation capability -- the Kremer O-ring signature (a low, hard-to-improve factor caps the product). Passive additive-vs-multiplicative fit is CONFOUNDED (Y is a weighted SUM of the same dims: R2_add=0.975 > R2_mult=0.947) and is NOT decisive.

amdahl.cross_field_import: Amdahl's Law (serial-fraction bound on parallel speedup)
amdahl.axis: compute dose (cost_proxy_usd relative to P0) holding retrieval-agent family
amdahl.caveats: Small-N fit (4 dose points); quality-as-throughput is a heuristic mapping. Two of the points (matched_P1, full P1) hold the architecture fixed and vary only budget, giving a genuine compute-dose contrast; P0 and P4 anchor the ends.
amdahl.verdict: On the compute-dose ladder (P0 1x -> matched_P1 3.2x -> P1 12.1x -> P4 17.5x), quality rises only 0.427 -> 0.495. Amdahl fit: parallelisable fraction f=0.124, so the SERIAL (non-parallelisable) fraction is 0.876 (~88%). Asymptotic quality at infinite compute is 0.488, which still falls 0.076 short of the per-query oracle ceiling (0.564): scaling parallel compute alone cannot reach what architecture selection achieves. Returns to orchestration compute are dominated by a large serial bottleneck.

nk.cross_field_import: NK fitness landscape / global epistasis (sum-of-marginals vs total)
nk.convention: single-component contribution = base - ablated = -ablation_delta; full_minus_baseline_gap uses the plain P0 pipeline as the all-components-off null; shortfall = sum_single - gap (>0 => sub-additive / substitutable components).
nk.verdict: Sum of single-component contributions vastly exceeds the net architecture advantage over the plain P0 baseline: P4 sum=0.126 vs full-minus-P0 gap=0.085 (shortfall 0.041, 1.5x); P5 sum=0.070 vs gap=0.043 (shortfall 0.027). Large positive shortfall = strong NEGATIVE / diminishing epistasis: components substitute rather than stack. The single load-bearing component is p4:no_triangulation (drop 0.0599). Orchestration components are individually necessary but jointly redundant -- consistent with one shared binding bottleneck (synthesis).

synthesis_constraint.triangulation_note: AGREEMENT: three independent cross-field lenses converge on ONE shared, non-parallelisable, sub-additive binding constraint, localised to synthesis/utilisation. (O-ring) the nominal min stage is retrieval-labelled (0.319), but the E5 intervention falsifies retrieval-AVAILABILITY as the fixable input (factual slope ~0, utilisation ceiling 0.32) -- the true binding factor is downstream synthesis-of-sources (grounding/recall), and raising a non-binding input caps the product exactly as Kremer predicts. (Amdahl) the serial non-parallelisable fraction of orchestration compute is 0.88, asymptote 0.488, still 0.076 short of the oracle ceiling -- parallel compute cannot buy the bottleneck away. (NK) single-component contributions sum to 0.126 but the net P4-over-P0 advantage is only 0.085 (shortfall 0.041): components substitute, not stack, consistent with all of them pushing on the SAME shared factor. Separately, the EVT closed form shows 88-99% of the raw oracle 'routability' headroom is a pure winner's-curse selection artefact. All four imports point the same way: orchestration returns are bounded because architectures contend for a single shared, serial, hard-to-improve synthesis/utilisation bottleneck -- not because any one component or more compute or better retrieval is missing. HONEST CAVEAT: the O-ring stage LABELS put factual grounding under 'retrieval'; the synthesis localisation rests on the E5/E14 utilisation evidence, not on stage quality alone.

portfolio_collective._note: Cross-field re-analysis: architecture PORTFOLIOS (Markowitz mean-variance, Pianka niche-overlap, Ladha correlated Condorcet jury, Cohen geometric-mean bet-hedging). Pure-CPU on on-disk data, NO API. Staging only (NOT canonical). Reuses the routability 3-judge matrix convention, loso source convention, sigma_run from variance_decomposition, and the judge_vs_gold mechanical-gold slice.

markowitz._method: Assets = 11 base architectures; states = 87 queries with all-11 3-judge-mean quality (mean of gpt52/claude_opus/claude_sonnet overall_score_recomputed); returns = per-query quality. Long-only fully-invested weights (w>=0, sum=1). Sigma = sample cross-query covariance (ddof=1). Sharpe = mean/query-risk (rf=0; returns are quality scores, not excess returns, so absolute Sharpe is large - the load-bearing comparison is blend-vs-single, not the level).

efficient_frontier_dominance.note: a single arch is Pareto-inefficient if some long-only portfolio matches its mean at strictly lower query-risk.

top_tier_diversifiability.note: mean of the 15 off-diagonal per-query return correlations among the top-tier arms; well below 1 => genuine diversification headroom among the good architectures.

out_of_sample_loso.note: weights fit on 4 sources, evaluated on the held-out source's queries (true OOS). The min-variance blend's diversification ratio (>1 in every fold) is the STRUCTURAL, overfit-proof OOS evidence. The max-Sharpe tangency blend overfits: it beats the best single arch in the 3 largest folds but the mean is dragged negative by the two smallest held-out folds (custom n=5, litqa2 n=10) where a single arch's held-out Sharpe is inflated by tiny-sample low variance; the median improvement is the robust summary.

markowitz.verdict: POSITIVE (diversification), in-sample structural: the min-variance blend cuts query-risk to 0.067, below the least-risky single architecture (0.076), with diversification ratio 1.29>1; it Pareto-dominates 8/11 single architectures and 10/11 single architectures are Pareto-inefficient (some blend matches their mean at lower risk). The tangency blend lifts in-sample Sharpe +13.2% over the best single arch (base_p4). Top-tier arms are only 0.46 mean-correlated, so the diversification headroom is genuine. OUT-OF-SAMPLE (leave-one-source-out): the min-variance blend's diversification ratio stays >1 in every fold (mean 1.494, min 1.2291) and its risk is below the least-risky single arch in 3/5 folds; the max-Sharpe tangency blend OVERFITS (median OOS Sharpe improvement 0.0846>0, but mean -4.2479 is dragged negative by the two smallest folds). Robust claim: blending lowers query-risk without sacrificing mean; chasing the max-Sharpe frontier point does not transfer.

pianka._method: Resource axes = 10 query bins (source x difficulty). Community = 6 top-tier arms. Each arm's utilisation = its win-share distribution across bins (argmax of per-query 3-judge-mean among the 6). Pianka (1973) overlap O_jk = sum(p_j p_k)/sqrt(sum p_j^2 sum p_k^2). Per-bin leader stability = fraction of 4000 sigma_run(=0.059) parametric perturbations that leave the bin's mean-leader unchanged. A routable/exclusive niche = a bin whose robust (stable>0.9, gap>2 noise-SE) leader is NOT the global champion.
pianka.verdict: ROUTER-NULL CONFIRMED: the global champion base_p1 wins 6/10 bins outright; the 4 bins led by a non-champion arm (base_p5,base_p6,base_p7) are ALL within the sigma_run noise floor (none has a stable, >2 noise-SE lead), so NO arm carves an exclusive/routable niche. Top-tier arms overlap 0.73 across bins (0.76 on non-singleton bins); the litqa2 bins are won by the champion, not an exclusive specialist. The per-source/per-bin leader rotation is sampling noise, not routable specialisation.

condorcet._method: Ladha (1992) correlated Condorcet jury. Gold = mechanical answer-correctness per (pattern,query) base report on the LitQA2+DeepSearchQA verifiable slice (reused from judge_vs_gold). Each judge's binary vote = thresholded overall_score_recomputed on the common report set scored by all 3 judges. p_i = accuracy vs gold; rho = pairwise correlation of ERROR indicators; correlated majority accuracy predicted by a beta-binomial (mean p_bar, intraclass corr rho_bar); N_eff = 3/(1+2*rho_bar) (same aggregation family as E3's n_eff=9/(3+2*sum phi)).
condorcet.threshold_sensitivity_note: PRIMARY uses a prevalence-matched vote rule (top-k flagged correct, k from the gold base rate) - it does NOT peek at which reports are gold-correct, so it is the apples-to-apples analogue of E3's raw-verdict phi and gives two-Claude error-corr 0.52 (vs E3 phi_opus|sonnet 0.512) and N_eff 1.57 (vs E3 1.65). The Youden robustness fits each judge's threshold SEPARATELY to gold, which mechanically decorrelates their errors (two-Claude corr drops to 0.03) and inflates N_eff to 1.80; N_eff stays well below 3 either way, but the correlated structure that corroborates n_eff is the non-gold-peeking (primary) rule.
condorcet.verdict: CORROBORATES n_eff: the two Claude judges are the most error-correlated pair (rho=0.52, vs the cross-family pairs), and the correlated-CJT effective independent-judge count is 1.57 (CI [1.4293, 1.7744]) - far below 3 and consistent with the independent E3 estimate n_eff=1.65. The beta-binomial correlated model predicts the observed 3-judge-majority-vs-gold accuracy (|err|=0.004) far better than the naive-independent CJT (|err|=0.055), confirming the votes are positively correlated, not independent.

geomean._method: Cohen (1966) bet-hedging: under query-domain (source) uncertainty the long-run deployment optimum is the geometric mean of per-source quality (penalises across-source variance), not the arithmetic mean. Per-source quality = mean per-query 3-judge quality within each of the 5 sources.

finer_granularity_robustness.note: Cohen's growth-rate optimum is the GM over environmental states; tested at source (5), source x difficulty bin (~10) and per-query (90) granularity. Per-query GM floors scores at 1e-6 so a single near-zero does not annihilate an arm.

geomean.verdict: NO RESHUFFLE at source granularity: arithmetic- and geometric-mean rankings are IDENTICAL (Spearman 1.00, 0 arms change rank); the deployment (bet-hedging) optimum is the SAME arm as the arithmetic optimum (base_p1). This is itself informative: base_p1's lead is NOT an artefact of averaging over volatile per-domain scores - it is top or near-top on every source (across-source sd 0.089, below lower-mean rivals), so it is robust to query-domain uncertainty, not a high-variance gamble. Finer-granularity robustness: per-bin GM top=base_p1 (no reshuffle), per-query GM top=base_p1 (reshuffles).

factor_model.question: Is 'report quality' ONE latent construct, or >=2 orthogonal factors (a 'form' factor = analytical_depth/organization/citation vs a 'truth' factor = factual_accuracy/attribution)?
factor_model.method: EFA (minres extraction) with promax OBLIQUE rotation (so inter-factor correlation phi is estimable) + Horn parallel analysis (1000 sims) for #factors; Kaiser>1 reported alongside. Primary unit = report x 9 dimension scores (met/total); robustness unit = report x 38 general binary criteria.
factor_model.adequacy: KMO 0.78-0.93, Bartlett p<1e-300 across solutions => data are factorable.

key_numbers.crit_opus_truth_sourcing_factor: factual_accuracy+citation_quality+attribution_quality -> one factor; phi to content bulk = 0.453

factor_model.verdict: NOT a clean single construct. A dominant general-quality factor exists, but a SEPARABLE second factor anchored by the sourcing/truth dimensions (factual_accuracy + citation_quality + attribution_quality) recurs in 2 of 3 single-judge solutions AND in the criterion-level solutions. Its correlation with the 'form/content' factor is weak-to-moderate and judge-dependent: r=0.108 (gpt52, near-orthogonal form vs truth), 0.453 (opus criterion-level), 0.553 (opus dimension-level). attribution_quality is the single most consistent outlier (lowest communality 0.217 and lowest loading 0.466 even in the disattenuated 1-factor solution). sonnet is the exception (unidimensional). Whether you 'see' 1 vs >=2 factors is driven by (a) judge and (b) averaging: averaging the panel inflates the general factor.
factor_model.supports_bounded_returns: YES, with caveats. When judge idiosyncrasy is preserved (gpt52), 'form' (organization/depth/citation) and 'truth' (factual_accuracy) sit on near-orthogonal factors (r=0.11 < 0.5). Orchestration that lifts the form factor need not move the weakly-coupled truth/sourcing factor => a factor-analytic mechanism for bounded returns and a caution against single-score leaderboards for the sourcing/factual dimensions.
factor_model.paper_statement: An exploratory factor analysis with parallel analysis over the 11-pattern x 3-judge verdict tensor finds that report quality is not a single latent construct: alongside a dominant general-quality factor, a separable 'sourcing/truth' factor anchored by factual_accuracy, citation_quality and attribution_quality recurs across the single-judge and criterion-level solutions, with attribution_quality the most consistent outlier (communality 0.22 even in the pooled one-factor fit). Its correlation with the 'form/content' factor is weak and judge-dependent - near-orthogonal under the GPT-5.2 judge (r=0.11) and only moderate under Claude Opus (r=0.45-0.55) - so a report can score highly on analytical depth, organisation and citation form while remaining flat on factual and attribution quality. This supplies a factor-analytic mechanism for bounded returns to orchestration and a caution against collapsing these weakly-coupled axes into one leaderboard number (the apparent unidimensionality of the pooled panel is partly an artefact of averaging judges, which disattenuates the inter-dimension correlations).

fail_reason_clusters.method: NOT-satisfied verdicts (satisfied==0) for 11 base patterns x 3-judge, reasoning>=15 chars; embedded with local all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (384-d, cosine-normalised, offline); KMeans at k=15/20/25 (primary k=20); representative terms via cluster-mean TF-IDF (1-2 grams), representative reasoning via nearest-to-centroid; dimension purity + normalised entropy per cluster; CROSS-DIMENSION flag = purity<0.45 AND >=3 dimensions each >=10%.

fail_reason_clusters.verdict: Most fail clusters are criterion-anchored (judge reasoning echoes the criterion wording -> high purity, e.g. 'author-analysis vs sourced material' 0.97, 'traceable to named sources' 0.90, 'citation formatting inconsistent' 0.97, 'multiple perspectives/schools of thought' 0.95, 'causal arguments unsupported' 0.94).
