A sixth max-entropy cluster is a degenerate 'no content' artefact (76% base_p9). Themes 1-5 are candidate UNDISCOVERED quality axes; the current 9-dimension rubric splits each of them across 3-4 dimensions, which both dilutes their signal and helps explain why single-dimension scores move less than the underlying failure would suggest.
fail_reason_clusters.paper_statement: Embedding and clustering the ~46k failing verdict rationales shows that while most failure clusters simply re-express a single rubric criterion, five recurrent themes cut cleanly ACROSS dimensions and are owned by no single one: temporal staleness (report misses the current state of the art / recent developments), poor epistemic calibration (no distinction between established and contested claims, no uncertainty signalling), descriptive-rather-than-mechanistic depth (facts catalogued but trade-offs and practical implications absent), non-specific 'Web Search Synthesis' placeholder sourcing, and a failure of decisiveness in directly answering the posed question. Together these cross-dimension themes account for roughly 42% of all failing verdicts, each currently scattered across three to four rubric dimensions, suggesting the 9-dimension rubric under-resolves several genuine quality axes. A sixth, maximally cross-dimensional cluster is not a quality axis at all but a degenerate empty-output artefact concentrated (76%) in the local 7B baseline (base_p9), a data-quality flag in its own right.

citation_network._purpose: Citation-network / domain-concentration analysis of df_citations.parquet (22,903 rows). $0 CPU. Non-canonical staging (NOT merged into canonical_numbers.json).
citation_network._data: data/analysis/df_citations.parquet (main, Bing backend) + df_citations_protocol_a.parquet (has backend col). Non-placeholder = category in {real_url,academic,suspicious}. Quality joins use mean over 3 judges {gpt52,opus,sonnet}.

concentration_findings.echo_chamber_verdict: NO severe echo chamber at architecture level: domain HHI is uniformly LOW (0.007-0.044) and Gini 0.25-0.48 across all 12 arms. Most concentrated arm is P2 (top-1 domain arxiv.org = 19.8% of cites, HHI 0.0435) - a mild arxiv over-reliance; every other arm's top domain is <11%.
concentration_findings.most_diverse: p3 (unique_ratio 0.727) and p11 (0.731) spread cites over the most distinct domains; p5 is least diverse (unique_ratio 0.406).
concentration_findings.placeholder_flag: Several 'strong' pipelines pad citations with fabricated/placeholder URLs: p4 61.6%, p3 59.1%, p8 56.8%, p5 50.8%, p10 37.0% of their citations are placeholders (vs p0/p6/p7/p1 <1%). Concentration/diversity above is computed on the NON-placeholder remainder.

academic_vs_web.finding: Web sources dominate every arm (54-79% web). Academic share is highest for the local 7B P9 (0.46) and single-round P8 (0.37); lowest for verbose web-scrapers P11 (0.21) and P5 (0.22). No arm is majority-academic.

diversity_vs_quality.level: per (pattern,query_id) cell; quality = mean over 3 judges
diversity_vs_quality.finding: Raw domain COUNT tracks quality only because it proxies citation volume: after controlling for n_cites, n_unique_domains->overall collapses to ~0 (partial -0.017, ns). But EVENNESS of sourcing (Shannon entropy) SURVIVES the volume control: shannon->citation_quality partial +0.444 (p=1e-46), ->overall +0.354, ->factual +0.267. Genuine source diversity predicts quality independent of citation count; citing more academic sources does NOT raise citation_quality (raw pearson +0.001, ns).

backend_confound.finding: DECISIVE search-backend confound (protocol-A subset): the Tavily backend produces an EXTREME echo chamber - 76.2% of ALL citations to arxiv.org, HHI 0.596 (near-monopoly), 89.5% academic - vs Bing 13.1% arxiv, HHI 0.025, 35.6% academic. Source concentration is driven far more by the retrieval backend than by the orchestration architecture; any cross-architecture diversity claim must hold backend fixed.

citation_network.verdict: No architecture is an echo chamber (HHI<=0.044); P2's mild arxiv over-reliance (~20%) is the ceiling. Source diversity DOES help quality, but only as EVENNESS (Shannon, partial +0.44 on citation_quality), not raw domain count (a citation-volume proxy) and not academic share. The dominant driver of source concentration is the SEARCH BACKEND (Tavily 76% arxiv / HHI 0.60), a confound that swamps architecture.

mvt_foraging._purpose: Charnov Marginal Value Theorem (MVT) over-foraging test: do iterative/reactive pipelines search past the point of diminishing marginal evidence yield, and does over-foraging buy any citation/quality gain? $0 CPU.
mvt_foraging._data_and_coverage: Within-run marginal-yield curves from checkpoints/<pattern>/<ts>/trace.json tool_calls (ordered by step_idx, n_results per retrieval verb). Arm-level effort/yield/score from canonical search_robustness + compute_ledger + per_dimension. COVERAGE CAVEAT: traces cover ~30/90 canonical qids for most pipelines (p0=43, p9=83); P11/P12 have NO usable traces. Raw n_results is verb-name-specific (NOT cross-architecture comparable) and does NOT dedup within run, so it OVERSTATES late-search value (any decline found is conservative). Per-call unique-URL dedup is not logged.

mvt_threshold_env_avg_yield.definition: Cross-source (environment) average marginal yield = grand mean n_results per 'search' call pooled across all 8 traced pipelines (n=4048 calls). MVT-optimal stop = when a pipeline's marginal new-doc yield falls to this environment average.

p1_iterative_rag.finding: STEEP diminishing returns: search 1 yields 8.3 docs, search 2 = 1.3, search 4 = 1.0 (8.3x collapse). ~93% of P1's search calls are issued AFTER marginal yield has already dropped below the environment average - a fixed-iteration loop that keeps foraging in an exhausted patch.

p6_reactive_interleaved.finding: Raw per-search yield does NOT decline (17.3 at step 1 -> 26.2 at step 13) because P6 targets a fresh subtopic each reactive step; raw n_results is not NEW-doc yield. MVT cannot be cleanly tested for P6 on raw counts (per-call dedup unlogged). P6 issues a FIXED 13 searches/run regardless of marginal value - no model-driven early stop.

p10_deep_researcher.finding: PATHOLOGICAL over-forager: all 17.4 search actions/run return 0 retrieved docs via the search verb (its docs arrive through tool_call/source_extract). 100% of its searches sit below the MVT stop, yet it keeps issuing up to 24. Extreme effort, near-zero search harvest.

arm_level_effort_vs_outcome.finding: DECISIVE consequence test (11 arms): searching MORE buys NOTHING. n_searches vs score pearson -0.336 (ns), vs citation_quality -0.178 (ns), vs factual -0.336 (ns), vs surviving citations -0.155 (ns), and vs docs actually retrieved +0.022 (ns). Every correlation is <=0 or null. The two heaviest foragers are the two worst outcomes-per-effort: P10 (24.4 searches -> score 0.336, LOWEST; 0.19 surviving citations/search) and P6 (13 searches -> 1.89 citations/search, same harvest efficiency as P0 which searches 4.6x less, at 18x P0's wall-clock).

mvt_optimal_stoppers.finding: The STRONG pipelines approximate the MVT stop: the top scorers forage little and quit early - P8 (1 search, 0.625, 34.8 citations/search), P4 (1 search, 0.640, 21.2/search), P7 (3 searches, 0.630), P1 (4 searches, 0.673). P0 reaches 0.488 in 2.8 searches, beating P10 (0.336) with 1/8th the foraging. Harvest efficiency (surviving citations per search) is INVERSELY related to search volume.

mvt_foraging.verdict: MVT holds as a diagnosis. (1) Where searches truly share a doc pool, marginal yield collapses fast (P1 8.3x over 4 searches; P5 widen->deepen 12.3x), and pipelines keep foraging past the environment-average stop (P1: 93% of searches). (2) The RL agent P10 is the extreme MVT violator: ~17 search actions/run, marginal new-unique-doc slope only +0.14 URLs per extra search (vs env avg 13.3), and it scores LOWEST. (3) Over-foraging correlates with ZERO quality/citation gain across 11 arms (all n_searches correlations <=0, ns). The strong architectures (P1/P4/P7/P8) implicitly obey MVT by stopping after 1-4 well-targeted searches. CAVEAT: raw-yield MVT cannot be tested per-call for P6 (fixed 13 searches, no dedup); trace coverage ~30/90 qids; P11/P12 untraced.

irt_dif._what: IRT differential-item-functioning (DIF): per-criterion judge x criterion interaction after controlling for report ability. Sharpens 'rating indeterminacy' from a global severity story to specific rubric ITEMS the judges read differently.
irt_dif.method: Two-stage anchored MFRM-DIF, pure CPU. Stage 1: refit the canonical 1PL many-facet Rasch model logit P(satisfied)=theta_report - b_criterion - s_judge on the same tensor (11 base patterns base_p0..base_p10, 3 core judges gpt52/claude_opus/claude_sonnet, satisfied_is_known, non-empty criteria; R=985, C=673, N=111869). This refit REPRODUCES the landed irt_tensor exactly (see reproduces_canonical). Stage 2: for each well-observed criterion (graded by all 3 judges, >=20 verdicts/judge; 38 general DRACO items, 108567 verdicts) estimate each judge's criterion-specific severity with report ability theta held FIXED as an offset (matched design: general criteria are graded by all 3 judges on the same reports, so judge severity is identified within-item). DIF_jc = criterion-specific severity minus that judge's GLOBAL severity; criterion DIF magnitude = across-judge range/rms of DIF_jc. Significance: unpenalised likelihood-ratio test H0(judge severities fixed at global) vs H1(free), df=2. Effect-size points use a MAP fit with a weak Gaussian prior (SD=2 logits) shrinking severities toward the global pattern, which bounds quasi-separation (e.g. gpt52 passes item a1deaebb52c2 0/985 times) and is CONSERVATIVE. BH-FDR across the 38 items.

reproduces_canonical.note: independent refit matches the landed irt_tensor to 4 dp => Stage-1 anchor validated.

irt_dif.units: logits (many-facet Rasch); higher judge severity = satisfies less. DIF range = max-min of judge deviations from their own global severity.

tensions.claim: The headline orchestration advantage over the single-pass baseline P0 is length/verbosity-confounded.
tensions.evidence: Raw 3-judge cluster-P0 = 0.145 [0.110,0.183] (excludes 0) collapses to -0.003 [-0.038,0.032] under the paper's own vintage-method length adjustment (slope 0.228/kword) and to +0.025 under query FE; only the log-words spec keeps it positive (+0.049). The GPT-5.2-only raw gap is already smaller (0.066 [0.038,0.094]).
tensions.contrast: The SCALE gap is length-robust: P0-P9 0.231 -> 0.113 [0.077,0.151] and cluster-P9 0.376 -> 0.110 [0.050,0.168] both stay positive across all length specs. So 'more scale helps' survives length control while 'more orchestration helps' (over P0) does not.

tensions.claim: Repeated sampling of the SIMPLE baseline can match/beat the orchestrated cluster (bounded returns).
tensions.evidence: best-of-12 on P0 with oracle (judge-max) selection = 0.495, exceeding the orchestrated cluster mean 0.470 by 0.025 (gap_best_of_N_to_cluster = -0.025). The best-of-k curve is almost entirely reproduced by a pure within-query judge-noise model.
tensions.contrast: The paper's intended bounded-returns point, but in tension with any reading that orchestration is a uniquely valuable source of quality; caveat: oracle selection is an UPPER bound, not realisable (cf. router_realisable null).

tensions.claim: Three lenses disagree on WHY the P1/cluster>P0 gain exists; jointly it is the most fragile headline claim.
tensions.evidence: (a) disentanglement: matched-budget clamp shrinks P1-P0 from 0.068 to 0.041 (n.s.), direct clamp effect -0.027 Wilcoxon p=0.053 => ~40% compute with a wide, sign-uncertain CI; (b) second_backbone gpt-4.1: the gain REPLICATES at 0.086 [0.027,0.148] (excludes 0); (c) length_adjusted: the 3-judge gain VANISHES to -0.003.
tensions.contrast: A backbone swap supports the gain being real; compute-matching and length-adjustment each erode it. The claim survives as directional/qualitative but not as a clean architecture-only effect.

tensions.claim: The family-clean headline leans on GPT-5.2, the ONLY panel judge validated against human gold -- but also the severest and the DIF driver.
tensions.evidence: judge_vs_gold: GPT-5.2 factual verdicts track human answer-correctness (AUC ~0.65, boot diff 0.073 [0.024,0.107]) while both Claude judges are near-chance. IRT: GPT-5.2 is the severest judge (s=+1.09) and, per irt_dif, its severe reading of citation/attribution items drives the largest item-level DIF.
tensions.contrast: Using GPT-5.2 as the load-bearing judge is defensible on validity grounds, but the same judge's severity and item-specific reading are what make the panel disagree (n_eff=1.65); the headline is thus partly a judge-choice. A robustness caveat, not a numeric contradiction.

meta_analysis.verdict: The evidence base is asymmetric. STRONG, multiply-robust: the SCALE effect (GPT-4o and larger local models beat the 7B baseline; survives length control, decontamination, backbone swap) and the SELECTION-CEILING story (oracle lifts citation not factual; utilisation ceiling ~0.32; realisable router cannot capture the headroom -- an INFORMATIVE null). FRAGILE: the orchestration-over-P0 gain (length-confounded, compute-borderline, though it replicates on gpt-4.1). Of 9 nulls, 4 are INFORMATIVE (router headroom, oracle-factual, E5-factual-flat, length-adjusted cluster gap) and 5 are UNDERPOWERED (both disentanglement clamps at n=29, both E10 noise contrasts at the tight 0.005 margin, E5 citation slope). Under-powered nulls should be reported as 'not established at this n', never as evidence of absence.

ablation_length_check._note: Checks whether ablation_p4_no_triangulation's delta (-0.0599, the figure the abstract's '~0.06' actually quotes) survives the same length-adjustment logic already applied to the P0-vs-cluster headline gap. Same judge pool and ovc field as build_numbers.py's ablations().
ablation_length_check.verdict: SURVIVES, PARTIALLY ATTENUATED. Removing triangulation shortens P4 reports by 110 words on average (60% of queries shorter), and the length-adjusted delta shrinks from -0.060 (raw, this judge pool) to -0.041 (at grand-mean length, 32% attenuation), but the adjusted 95% CI still excludes zero. So part of the abstract's quoted ~0.06 ablation effect is a length artefact, similar in kind (though smaller in share) to the ~40% compute confound already reported for the P1 matched-budget disentanglement probe -- the triangulation-removal effect on quality is real but the raw figure overstates the pure-content-removal share by roughly this attenuation.
